utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is Monday, 9th of March, 2009. Good afternoon to the accused, and in particular to Mr. Petkovic, who's back with us today. Good afternoon to the Defence counsel, all the OTP representatives, the Registrar, and all the people assisting us. We are starting ten minutes later than usual because the previous Trial Chamber had worked later than scheduled. I really insist on everybody finishing on time, because when I have a hearing, I make sure I don't go over time because this is bound to have consequences for those following us. The Presiding Judges have to be able to conduct hearings in good time. This being said, I'll first ask the Registrar to give us some IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Pinjuh, Dragan. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC939. The list submitted by 4D shall be given Exhibit IC940. The list submitted by the Prosecution shall be given Exhibit IC941. And 2D has submitted objection to the Prosecution's documents tendered via Witness 2D-AB. This list shall be given Exhibit IC942. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have three rulings to hand down; the first related the Prlic Defence request for overstepping the number of words. There was a confidential annex to the request regarding a witness and a request for being allowed to use more words than the number usually allowed. Further to the practical direction of the Tribunal regarding the length of motions and briefs, dated the 16th of September, 2005, one -- a motion may not be longer than 3.000 words. A party is, however, allowed to seek leave to use more words than the usual word limit, but has to reason its request, justifying exceptional circumstances for longer briefs or motions. The Trial Chamber notes that the instant motion contains 5.506 words and is longer than the allowed amount of words. The Trial Chamber cannot deviate from the general -- or cannot abide by this practice by the Prlic Defence, which is to file a longer motion whilst asking, in the same motion, for leave to use more words. The Trial Chamber is of the view that the Prlic Defence should have sought leave to increase the word limit before the Trial Chamber before it filed its motion. Furthermore, in the view of the Trial Chamber, the Prlic Defence failed to demonstrate the presence of exceptional circumstances that would allow for a longer filing. Therefore, the Trial Chamber denies the request for exceeding the word limit and decides not to look into the Prlic motion. It is for the Prlic Defence to file new filings, complying with the authorised word limit. Second ruling regarding notice of the testimony of the witness who's supposed to start his testimony today. After deliberation, the Trial Chamber decided to grant the Stojic Defence, as part of the examination-in-chief, one hour and fifteen minutes. The other accused will be given 45 [as interpreted] minutes. And the Trial Chamber has decided to allot the OTP, for their cross-examination, one hour and fifteen minutes. There seems to be a mistake in the transcript. For the other accused, it is 40 minutes, not 45. Third ruling, regarding Witness Nenad Sandzic [as interpreted]. The Trial Chamber decided to grant the Stojic Defence, for their examination-in-chief of the witness, one hour. The other Defence teams will have 30 minutes, and the OTP will have one hour. However, regarding the possibility for the Praljak Defence to examine the witness under Rule 92 ter, the Trial Chamber decided not to grant time to the Praljak Defence for the witness. The Praljak Defence will have to call the witness themselves when they begin their case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. This last ruling was taken by a majority of Judges. I had a dissenting opinion. I wanted to keep on the same track for the sake of synergy and time-saving, and I felt quite positive that it would have been possible to better use this time as part of what was planned. That's the reason why I was not in favour of the last decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will file a separate opinion regarding this decision after thoroughly reflecting on the issue. The fact that an accused calls a witness as part of the case of another accused may bring about conflicts of interest between the parties, the Defence teams. Therefore, I believe it is suitable for each accused to call their own witnesses as part of -- they see logical in their Defence strategy without calling them as part of another accused's case. These were the three rulings. We're going to have the witness brought in. Please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I would just like to correct the transcript. On page 3, line 15, the name of the witness should read "Nedzad Cengic," and in the record it says "Nenad Sandzic." It should be "Nedzad Cengic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I always had a tough time with the names, but we ought to have them properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please state your surname, first name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Tihomir Majic, born on the 14th of May, 1958, Rudo municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am retired now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are retired from the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, an army pensioner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the army. And what was your rank when you retired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you had an opportunity to testify before a court of law or is this going to be the first time you're going to testify to the events that took place in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I'm testifying before a court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read out the solemn declaration handed over to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Please be seated. A few words by way of explanation from me, but I believe that Ms. Nozica has already explained it all to you, but you never know. You will first answer questions by Ms. Nozica, and she may submit to you documents in so doing. Once this is done, the other Defence counsel, who are seated behind her or next to her, may have questions for you as well, if they think it's necessary as part of their own cross-examination. As to the Prosecutor, I think it's going to be Madam Prosecutor, she's seated on your right-hand side, she also will have questions for you as part of her cross-examination. You have four Judges in front of you. They may at any time ask questions of you, but as a rule we prefer putting questions to documents in order to save time, not to have to look for the document again. Sometimes it's quite strenuous to testify, especially if this is a first for you. That's why you're going to have 20-minute breaks every 90 minutes. You are now a witness of the Court. No doubt you'll come back tomorrow into this courtroom, but you're not to have any contact whatsoever with anybody until your testimony is over. Do endeavour to be precise in your answers. If you fail to understand any question, do not hesitate to seek clarification, and the one asking you may reformulate it, even if the Judges are asking you questions, because they're not perfect, they don't know everything, and sometimes they're not able to express their questions properly. So do not hesitate to ask the Judges to reformulate their questions. If at any time you're not feeling well, just raise your hand and we'll have a break immediately so that you can have a rest. So all this for the testimony to take place as smoothly as possible, in the interests of the Accused Stojic, who's calling you, and also in the interests of justice. You may proceed, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Majic.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to go through your CV now, but I'd like to start off by asking you whether, in the official documents, you used your nickname, "Tiho."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, fine. Now, I'm going to go briefly through your CV, and you can tell us at the end whether what I've read out is correct, so that we can move forward. The Secondary School of Construction is one you graduated from in 1976 in Vukovar; is that right? And you had a construction company of your own from 1980 to 1990 in Grude. At the end of 1991, you were appointed to the Crisis Staff of Grude municipality, and you worked there procuring materiel and technical equipment. When the Main Staff was established, and that was roughly in April 1992, the warehouse and depot formed part of the Main Staff, and you continued working as a warehouse operator. In May 1993, this warehouse or, rather, the logistical base, the Central Logistics Base, as it was called, became part of the Procurement Sector, and under the Defence Department. You continued working in the Logistics Base as a warehouse-keeper. In May 1993, you were appointed to another duty, the deputy assistant of the head of the Defence Department, in the Procurement Sector -- Procurement and Production Sector. And from May 1993, that same date, until 1997, you mostly worked in -- on jobs concerning construction. In 1997, you retired. Is all that information correct, Mr. Majic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, all the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, can you tell the Trial Chamber who and when appointed you to the Crisis Staff of Grude municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I was appointed by the Municipal Council. I was appointed by them to the Crisis Staff of Grude municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: 1991, towards the end of the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber why the Crisis Staff was set up in the first place?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: When the Serb Army attacked the municipality of Ravno and deployed their tanks in Kupres municipality, everything that went on in the Republic of -- and in view of everything that went on in the Republic of Croatia, the Crisis Staff was set up in Grude municipality for defence purposes, to defend us from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you given any assignments in that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: In the Crisis Staff, my assignments were to procure and store materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did the Grude municipality have any weaponry which could be used had an attack by the Serb Army taken place?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: At that time, the Territorial Defence of Grude municipality had its own weapons, but prior to the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina those weapons were seized by the JNA, which meant that we did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If I've understood you correctly, when you were appointed to the Crisis Staff, when it was established at the end of 1991, that same Crisis Staff had no weaponry.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: That is right, it did not have any weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please, what was your first task when you joined the Crisis Staff? What did you do first upon your appointment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: When I was appointed, the first thing we did was to make a list of all the hunting weapons in Grude municipality; that is to say, we called up -- we called upon the citizens to report their weapons so that we could make a record of them, and we made some devices like Molotov cocktails and so on to be able to deal with the enemy, and then we started to purchase automatic rifles as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How did you purchase the automatic weapons, and did you? Did you and how?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: At the level of the municipality, we would call upon all the citizens who wished to purchase weapons and who had the money to purchase weapons and could do so, and we collected about 120.000 German marks in that first stage, and the president of the Executive Council went and procured the weapons. And when the weapons arrived, they were stored in my warehouse. And as soon as I received a list of persons who had purchased the weapons, I distributed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say the weapons came to the warehouse. Did you have a warehouse, and if so, which warehouse or depot? And we're still talking about that first stage when you were in the Crisis Staff of Grude municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. My warehouse was at the tobacco station, which is located in the centre of town, the centre of Grude, and after the Serbs left, we moved that warehouse to the Drinovci area, and that was from mid-April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say that you relocated to Drinovci. Where in Drinovci?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: In a forest there. It's called "the forest," "suma," and there was a road there, and we hitched up some trailers where we stored goods that were not supposed to get wet. We kept them dry in those trailers and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said the so-called "forest." Was it really a forest or was it just called a forest?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was out in the open, a real proper forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, why did you relocate the warehouse to this forest out in the open?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: We moved the warehouse to prevent the Serbs from shelling us, as they had done the previous one, so we thought that this would be a provisional, temporary measure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the issue of dates is absolutely essential for the Judges. As I understand it, when the Serbs attacked, the Grude Crisis Staff decided to get armed, and you played a part in it. If I understand properly, this was during 1991, early 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At some point in time, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was recognised internationally by the international community. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You knew that. When the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had legal existence, did the Grude Crisis Staff call the government led by Mr. Izetbegovic in order to say, Look, the Serbs are attacking us. We need weapons. You must send us troops, weapons, food, et cetera? Was that done or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, I was just a warehouse-keeper, so in my job description, that wouldn't have been part of it, so I didn't feel the need to do that. That wasn't my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean you can't answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, in response to my question of why the warehouse was relocated to the forest, you said, among other things, that you didn't think it would last long. What did you have in mind? What wouldn't last long?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: The war, that the war wouldn't last long.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me, please, how long did the warehouse stay in the forest, up until when?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollections, it remained there until September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And when did you work in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I worked in the warehouse until mid-May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, during the time the Crisis Staff was established for Grude municipality, did you have any contact whatsoever with the other crisis staffs in the other municipalities with respect to weapons procurement, agreement about how to procure weapons, and things of that kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of 1992, we did not have any contacts between the municipalities, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what happened at the beginning of 1992 to change that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: In 1992, the Inter-Municipality Crisis Staff was established, and my warehouse became part of the regional warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, that became the regional -- it became the regional warehouse.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And were you still the warehouse-keeper in that same warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I continued to be the warehouse-keeper.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, what happened in April 1992 with that warehouse of yours?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: In April 1992, the Main Staff was established, and then my warehouse became part of the Logistics Base of the Main Staff, but I continued to do my job and work as a warehouse-keeper.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, after the beginning of the conflict with the Serbs on the territory of HZ-HB, did you receive in your warehouse any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you kept working at your job of store-keeper, so does that mean that you were just doing manual work, or you would take a rifle from one room to take it to another room, or you give it to somebody, or does that mean that you had more intellectual work, where you have to manage the entire logistics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just receive the goods and issue the goods, according to decisions and lists. That was my job, basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, after the beginning of the conflict with the Serbs on the territory of HZ-HB, did you receive any materiel and technical equipment or weapons from some other source?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: When the HVO repelled the Serbs or, rather, when we took control of some of the barracks that had been held by the Serbs, then I received quite a lot of materiel and technical equipment, which I stored and then, according to orders, issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do I understand you to say that the weapons came from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was weapons that were there after the Serbs had left the barracks. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, who was your superior officer, Mr. Majic, after the warehouse in April, as you said, of 1992 moved to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: My superior from mid-1992, until July, was Mr. Bruno Stojic, who was the assistant commander for logistics in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, everything is going very fast. You've just said something. When the JNA left, you said, you somehow managed the weapons they'd left behind. We've heard a lot of witnesses so far, and I was under the understanding that when the JNA left their barracks, they took everything with them, there was no weapon left. And now -- I've been in this Tribunal for nearly six years, and this is the first time I hear what you've just said; namely, that the JNA left weapons behind. So I'm trying to understand. Are you sure that the JNA left weapons behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's like this: The JNA didn't leave of its own free will, of its own accord, voluntarily. There was an offensive, and I do think that part of the materiel and technical equipment remained, stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now we can understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, let's clarify that. When did this, as you called it, offensive take place? When did the conflict between the HVO and BH Army take place? Can we clarify that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No, not the BH Army, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I do apologise. It's my mistake. Not the BH Army, but the HVO and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: That happened in April, when we took control, as we were told -- 1992, that is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: April 1992. What about the TO weapons that was in storage units belonging to the TO? What about when that was seized from all the municipal TOs by the JNA? When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: That occurred prior to the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina, meaning early 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, these are two different things; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the one hand, the TO weapons being taken from TO storage units or warehouses, and, on the other, weapons being seized after the HVO set free or liberated the barracks previously held by the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A while ago, you replied by saying that between mid-1992 and July 1992, Bruno Stojic was your superior. He was assistant commander for logistics in the Main Staff. Do you perhaps remember whether that was in mid-1992 or could you more specific than that and remember the actual month?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: It was between April and the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Then who became your superior after July 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: After July, Mr. Bruno Stojic was replaced by Mr. Ante Jelavic as assistant commander for logistics in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For how long did Mr. Jelavic continue to be your superior in that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: He remained as my superior up until mid-May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. And what happens then, mid-May 1993? What happened to the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: The warehouse became part of the Procurement and Production Sector, which itself was attached to the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you change jobs in mid-May? Were you appointed to a different position?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I was appointed assistant head for procurement and production with the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Deputy assistant with the Procurement and Production Sector?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And who was appointed assistant head?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ante Jelavic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, following mid-May 1993, following your appointment as deputy assistant head of the Procurement and Production Sector, what did your work comprise?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I was working more with the Construction Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So following May 1993, did you have any more contacts or anything to do with the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, can you now please explain to the Chamber if you knew how materiel and technical equipment was procured. At first when you were with the Crisis Staff as well as later when the warehouse became a regional warehouse and eventually became the Logistics Base and, as such, part of the Main Staff, did you know anything about how MTS, materiel and technical equipment, was actually procured?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: During the first stage of this operation, early 1992, I did know how this was done. We bought all the equipment with our own money, and the equipment was sourced from a number of different countries. I remember that first stage, when we got some equipment from Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about later on, when the warehouse became a regional one, the central warehouse? Do you know how procurement worked at that point?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No. After this, I no longer knew anything about how weapons were procured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may. Witness, just a small question. You said, "We bought with our own money." Whose money would that have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The money of the citizens of Grude municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, what about municipal crisis staffs or HVO municipal crisis staffs, which is what they later became; did they get materiel and technical equipment directly for HVO units in their own area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Each staff got equipment for the units and for the crisis staffs separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about this materiel and technical equipment; were any documents produced about that or did it go straight to your warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about materiel and technical equipment at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You first worked as a warehouse-keeper with the Municipal Crisis Staff and later with the Logistics Base. Were there any warehouses in HVO units at the time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, each unit had its own warehouse. Rather, recruitment districts had assistance -- assistant commanders for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mentioned recruitment districts or areas, so would that apply to brigades and all the rest; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the brigades --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, in order to avoid this problem, can you please wait until I finish asking my question before you start your answer. You said recruitment districts or areas. What about the other brigades, battalions and companies, well, to the extent that you can tell?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know all the units had their own warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did they all have assistant commanders for logistics?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: That is understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, can you explain to the Trial Chamber how you distributed MTS or materiel and technical equipment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I would get a distribution order from my own superior, and then I would act upon it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you the only one with the power to have MTS distributed, the only one in that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I had a deputy too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Marinko Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you still the one who was really in charge of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was the one in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, were there ever any requests for MTS by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were three different ways in which this happened. The BH Army would send a request directly to municipal staffs. If municipal staffs didn't have all the equipment, they would go to our central warehouse to get more supplies. Then there were situations in which they would address a certain warehouse directly -- or, rather, there would be a distribution order dispatched to this warehouse. They would then go to this warehouse, having seen my superior first. And the third way was from MORH, to have equipment delivered to my warehouse, and the distribution order would say that the equipment was meant for the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about this third channel or the third way? When the MTS would arrive at your warehouse from MORH, is this the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say the distribution order would then clearly state that this was equipment for the BH Army; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, how long did your warehouse continue to issue MTS, weapons and other such items, for the purposes of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: For as long as I remained in my position as warehouse-keeper, so until mid-May; that is, at least as far as I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just tell me the year again?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll try to ask you a specific question, if you can remember that. Can you remember anyone from the special MUP unit coming over -- the BH special MUP unit from Sarajevo, to pick up MTS?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this one situation. It struck me as slightly strange. Sarajevo was surrounded at the time, and yet someone from Sarajevo was now here to pick up MTS. That was mid-February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, can you perhaps remember if anyone came from the 2nd Corps of the BH Army to pick up MTS?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: People from the 2nd Corps came several times, but what I remember is when they came in early May and picked up quite a considerable amount of MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say "early May." Which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, how exactly did you technically issue MTS to members of the BH Army? Was there a different procedure that was in place, as opposed to the one used when you were issuing MTS to HVO units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: There was no difference, in terms of procedure. We used the same procedure for both. They would dispatch a request to my superior. My superior would then issue me with a distribution order, and then I would execute the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, I'll first ask the usher's assistance. We need our binder of documents to be handed to the witness. We shall now be going through a number of documents in relation to what we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, before we look at the documents, you said something which awakened my interest. You said that you had been extremely surprised to see somebody from the MUP arrive in mid-February of 1993 concerning MTS. That person had walked away with some equipment. I understand why you were surprised. Had you heard of those events which had taken place in Prozor in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I did not mention any event in Prozor myself. But another reason I was surprised is because they came from Sarajevo, and Sarajevo at the time was surrounded by the Serbs, and that's why I was surprised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When this person came in February 1993, as far as you know, had there been a conflict between the ABiH and the HVO by then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, so there had been clashes. How can you explain that the "enemy," in inverted commas, is being procured by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't consider the BH Army to be a real enemy, or at least I didn't. It was a series of unfortunate coincidences. There was a group of people, and this was something that went back to the former Yugoslavia, who were always into causing accidents, trying to get more convenience for themselves and less convenience for everyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you were concerned, it was a clique or small group of people from the former Yugoslavia who were behind the clashes between the HVO and the ABiH; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, they had their own agents that they were infiltrating, their mission being to bring about clashes between the Croats and the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when the person from the MUP comes, you did not consider this person to be an enemy. Was this person a friend or was he a fighter like you? Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were other warehouse-keepers in charge of MTS from those units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you did not answer my question. Those people who come and pick up the equipment for the ABiH, as far as you were concerned, were these brothers-in-arms, were these friends, were these people like you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Their insignia told me that they were members of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, if we could please try to shed some light on this. The Presiding Judge asked you several times whether, when those people came from the 2nd Corps and the special MUP units in Sarajevo, whether you consider them as enemies. Who were they fighting, both when they were with the 2nd Corps and in Sarajevo? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I personally did not consider them to be my enemies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on to the documents that I have here. Can we please first go to P586. It's the first document in your binder. Mr. Majic, this is a decision on the basic structure of the Defence Department, dated September 1992, signed by Mr. Mate Boban. Let me first ask you if before you were proofed for this case you'd ever set eyes on this document.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at point 8, and we're going to look at the place of this central warehouse, where it is in establishment terms. So take a look at point 8. You said that as of May 1993, you were the deputy assistant to the head in the Sector for Procurement and Production, and here we see in point 8 on page 2 a list of eight administrations within that same sector in September 1992. Now, did your logistical base belong to one of these administrations, and did it belong to the sector at all?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: My logistical base did not belong here, did not come under this sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now let's look at document 2D, the next document, 00567. 2D00567 is the number, and that should be the next document in your binder. And this is a decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department, dated the 10th of July, 1992. And on page 4, look at the Sector for Procurement and Production, and the date is the 17th of October. It's the 17th of October, 1992. That's how the transcript should read. Now, we have the structure of the sector here, and within that structure, in October, was there a logistics base in any of these administrations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No, there's no logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now let's look at another document on establishment and organisation. It is P2477, and this is a decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department, dated the 20th of May, 1993. And I'd like to ask you to take a look at page 3 once again, point 7, in which we have a breakdown of the administrations and everything that made up the Sector for Procurement and Production within the Defence Department. Now, Mr. Majic, on page 4, do we see the appearance for the first time here, the head of the Central Logistics Base, and does that coincide with what you know, that as of May 1993, this Logistics Base became part of the Procurement and Production Sector of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, look at the next document, please, which is 2D01024, and just tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. This is a pass dated the 30th of June, 1992, signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic, and I'd like to ask you now, Mr. Majic, whether Mr. Bruno Stojic during this period was your superior, and tell Their Honours, please, which post he held or what the title of his position was, and we can see that from this document.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: At the time, he was my superior. He was the assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're talking about the 30th of June, 1992, so it would be a good idea to repeat what we've already said. Who was your superior as of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: My superior was Mr. Ante Jelavic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, let's look at the next document, which is 2D01 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, it might be useful to have in the record [indiscernible] as I'm saying it, that will be it, that the previous document had the number 2D01024.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. 2D01 -- you're right, 2D01024. I saw the number and thought it was the right one, but thank you for putting me right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So would you take a look at the document, once again, 2D01253 this time, and tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, just briefly, here we have nine receipts making up this document, and two entries for goods coming in; receipts for the 26th of February, 1992, and go up to the 30th of March, 1993. And this first receipt, number 1/7 -- 117, we see your signature there, and we see on the right who took over the MTS, the materiel and technical equipment. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what this document represents? What is it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a document which indicates how the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina purchased weapons in Slovenia and shipped them to the Drinovci warehouse and then -- well, Grude municipality, and then pursuant to an agreement with the minister, Mr. Delimustafic, and Mr. Stojic, that weaponry was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, so we're talking about the 26th of February, 1992, there, and we're referring to the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, do you happen to know Mr. Bahto Hamid?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Yes, Bahto Hamid. Now, after this receipt number 117, we have a series of other receipts. I'd just like you to confirm, if you can, to the Trial Chamber that all these nine receipts tell us which people were concerned with this and that they were all Bosniak Muslim names.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, would you explain something to the Trial Chamber, and in order to do that, look at the penultimate page of the document. In English, it is 2D75-0087 and 0088; and in the Croatian, it is 2D71-0331 and 0332. Now, Mr. Majic, here we have goods entered and we can see that it came from the MUP of Slovenia, goods received from and received by Mr. Tihomir Majic, but we see the date is the 7th of April, 1992. Now, from the previous receipts, we can see all this MTS, materiel and technical equipment, was distributed from the 26th of February up until the 30th of March, 1993 [as interpreted], and could you explain to the Trial Chamber how come that the entry of goods was entered only on the 7th of April, 1992, was recorded then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: The standard practice for the first stage was this: I would be -- I would be given a copy of the outgoing document, and then later on I would record it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to make a correction. Page 27, line 2, should read "March 1992" and not "1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, if I understood you correctly, you received a copy with the goods, a receipt saying that the goods had been sent. You would be given a copy, and only once you received the original would you enter the goods into the document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, I'd like to move on to another set of documents which would tell us something about what you told us a moment ago; that is to say, the way in which goods were distributed from your warehouse, the MTS, for the requirements of the BH Army. And in order to do that, let us take a look at the first document, which is 2D00522. Now, Mr. Majic, let me say by way of introduction that this is an independence battalion for the defence of Mostar. It says, "The HVO" on the document, and it is a request for ammunition, dated the 13th of July, 1992, and the request is signed by Arif Pasalic, and it is sent by the HVO Municipal Staff of Mostar. Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber whether that was one of the ways in which the weapons were issued? And you've already explained to us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is how they contacted the Municipal Staff. And if there wasn't enough MTS in the Municipal Staff, then this would be furnished by us or, rather, the Logistics Base would provide what was needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, you said if there was not enough materiel and technical equipment. Now, during the time that you were the warehouse-keeper, that is to say, from the beginning of 1992 until May 1993, did you have enough MTS to supply these requests by the BH Army and also to satisfy the requests made by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: We always had a shortage of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now let's look at the next document, which is 2D0052 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let's stay with document 2D0522. This is a document signed by Arif Pasalic on the 13th of July, 1992. As far as you know, on that day, on the 13th of July, 1992, was the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina an independent state, recognised as such by the international community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be quite frank, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know. Regarding this document we have in front of us, this is the first time I've seen it, but does this show that Mr. Arif Pasalic belongs to the Independent Battalion for the defence of Mostar of -- belonged to the HVO Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this document show that Mr. Arif Pasalic asked the HVO headquarters -- or, rather, sent them a letter regarding weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, it does show that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this Arif Pasalic the one who is going to find himself responsible for the ABiH in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, just to make things quite clear for the transcript, this request is sent to the HVO of the Municipal Staff of Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Majic, during the examination-in-chief, you spoke about these cases, and they said sometimes they would contact the municipal staffs, and if the municipal staffs did not have enough, did not have the quantity specified and "... we had them, then the Logistics Base where I worked would supply the goods." Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now we're going to deal with similar documents, just to lay the foundations for that, and look at the next document, 2D00523. This is, as we can see from the heading, from the top part -- it says: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." We see the ARBiH, the BH Army, and the 1st Mostar Brigade. The date is the 31st of October, 1992, and here we can also see that it is signed by the commander, Mr. Arif Pasalic. And this request once again went through the HVO Municipal Staff Mostar, Logistics Department for the Technical Service. Can you confirm, Mr. Majic, that this once again is the same procedure as we saw a moment ago and explained earlier on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just tell us whether it's the same procedure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same procedure as in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at the next document, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Witness, this Arif Pasalic, in the previous document the signature must have been in his name, because they're not the same signatures. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But am I wrong in saying that back in July Mr. Pasalic was in the HVO, and in October he was with the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Looking at both documents, one could even believe it was the same typewriter that was used, but that should be checked by an expert. But besides that, do we realise that we have the same addressee in both documents, HVO, Opsinski [phoen], Stozer, Mostar? So is it the same addressee? Sorry for the spelling, the way I pronounce names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's precisely it, the same addressee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we believe that this was the same typewriter that was used? Look.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't think so. Very well, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But Mr. Majic, you're certainly no graphologist, no handwriting expert. Therefore, you can't be certain whether it is or not, in fact; am I right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's move on to 2D524. Tell me as soon as you've found it, sir.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The document bears the date the 12th of December, 1992, if I may draw your attention to the date. It is a request to the municipal headquarters of the HVO, Logistics Section, signed by Mithad Hajdar, commander. It reads: "Request for equipment and materiel. Given the fact that our brigade has been carrying out combat operations in the Igman area on lifting the blockade around the city of Sarajevo, we address you with this request for delivery of the following MTS that is now required." Different kinds of weapons are listed there, and so on and so forth. Mr. Majic, is this one of those requests that were dispatched to municipal staffs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please move on to the next aspect, as you said, a way in which the BH Army addressed the HVO, you, personally, in order to have MTS delivered. Can you please now go to 2D1252. Mr. Majic, the electronic copy of this document is not particularly legible, but the date is the 29th of September, 1992. We don't see the addressee. The text reads: "Based on the agreement between Mr. Arif Pasalic, commander of the 1st Mostar Brigade, commander of the Operative Group for South-East Herzegovina, Mr. Poljak, Drago, and Mr. Pizovic, Bajro, commander of the Bregava Brigade, Stolac, on taking offensive action with the objective of clearing of the territory in the direction of Nevesinje, please approve the following equipment: Mortar shells, artillery rounds," the types are specified, "and ammunition," with the types requested specified. The document is not signed but we see the names there, Arif Pasalic, Drago Poljak, Bajro Pizovic. Mr. Majic, did you receive requests like this at your own logistics base, and how, if so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: There were numerous requests like this, many, many requests like this. One of the ways was to address my superior, who would then issue the distribution order and order the -- order hand-overs of MTS. Sometimes copies arrived of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you're telling us about the procedure. Requests such as this one would be forwarded to your superior; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And he would then draw up a distribution order; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But sometimes the distribution order would be a document like this, showing exactly who is submitting the request?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then based on the distribution order, you would distribute equipment and materiel to whoever had their name clearly displayed in the distribution order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please move on to the next document, and this is now again something about the distribution of MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. We started late today, and I thought we -- [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's have a break now, a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, can you please now look at 2D00955. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber what this is about? This is a certificate of the HVO, Municipal Staff Grude, the 29th of April, 1992. Can you explain to the Chamber, based on what you know, do you know these persons? What exactly is this document about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: This is the Sarajevo TO Staff, and they are addressing directly the Grude Municipal Staff. It is clear that this gentleman, Ante Busic, is issuing certain equipment, and a gentleman who at the time was commander, Nikola Nikolic, approves this so that the goods can be taken to Sarajevo without encountering any obstacles, and the transport leader, as it reads, is Enver Baskovic. I know Mr. Ante Busic, and I know Mr. Nikola Nikolic personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, this document shows that Mr. Busic issued this equipment from 1 to 9; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And this commander, 1st Lieutenant Nikola Nikolic, issued this certificate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, to transport this merchandise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Majic, do you know if it was necessary to issue these authorisations every time weapons were transported at the time? For example, you issuing equipment -- this isn't you in this document, but when you or anyone else did that, was a pass required, regardless of the fact whether it was your logistics base that was issuing equipment, or whether equipment was merely moving through HZ-HB territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Each transport that occurred needed a pass or a permit to pass through an area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, you said during your examination-in-chief that there were cases when weapons were obtained for the benefit of the BH Army in the following way: The Defence Ministry of the Republic of Croatia would deliver the goods to your logistics base, but the weapons would be clearly marked as either for the BH Army or for the armed forces. Can we now please go to a series of documents discussing that, the first being 2D00630. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Please explain. This is a request dated the 10th of April, 1992, issued by the Defence Ministry of the Republic of Croatia, stating the kind of equipment required, saying that this is for the 106th Orasje Brigade of the HVO, BH armed forces, and then a list with the names of persons who are supposed to take delivery. How exactly did you take delivery of this equipment, and on what basis did you then go on and distribute it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I would first receive this in my warehouse, and then these gentlemen would bring a distribution order. I would then act on it and distribute equipment with the proviso that all of the distribution orders were produced by my superior, Mr. Jelavic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you received this equipment, did you also receive an order like this showing exactly who the equipment was for?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I always received a copy of the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's fine. Can we now move on to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A small detail, Witness. Ms. Nozica didn't ask you about it. This is a document from Mr. Cermak, the assistant defence minister, so he's an important person of authority in the Republic of Croatia, and the date is 10th of October, 1992. This is ordering materiel listed from 1 to 8. I am interested in the second line. It says: "HVO, 106th Brigade, Orasje BiH armed forces." Back in October 1992, did the BiH have a unit or not in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there was only the HVO 106th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what the title appears to be indicating, but there were Muslims too or, rather, Bosniaks in that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there were also Muslims, you say. I can see that it is written "BiH armed forces." This is a document from Mr. Cermak. He could be a witness, because he's here anyway. Does this not show that for the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, the 106th Brigade is part of the BiH armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a complex question. You might not be able to answer it. You were a military. As such, when you look at this document -- or could the one reading the document conclude that for General Lieutenant Cermak, the 106th Brigade is part of the BiH armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now move on to the next document, please, and the document bears the following number -- or, rather, it's a rather different document, in terms of who is receiving weapons, 3D00436.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, again a request signed by Mr. Cermak, the same date as the previous one, but it reads: "For issuance of materiel resources for the needs of the central background base Grude, at the disposal of the BH Army Foca-Gorazde."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, could all the microphones not being used be switched off, please. There is a lot of interference and noise. We can't keep on interpreting because we can't hear counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in order for you to receive the weapons, in order for you to receive a copy of this request. What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: We would take delivery of the MTS, and then there would be a distribution order from my superior and we would follow that. As a result, we would distribute and issue MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw the warning from the interpreters. I will make sure that I'm facing the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please move on to the next document, 3D00437. Again, a request by Mr. Cermak, or he's the person who signed the document. The date this time around is the 16th of October, 1992. Was this request followed -- or this order followed in the same way as all the previous ones as you have described to us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same method was applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, we see the name Sahinpasic, Senad, written towards the bottom of the page. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber whether you're familiar with this person and whether this person, for the purposes of the BH Army, came to see you in order to get weapons? And if so, how many times?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinpasic came several times to Grude to get MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was that for purposes of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, every time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. We see the timeline here in these. And the next one is 2D00898.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, in this document, we can see that Lieutenant General Cermak wrote "BH Army" and "HVO." I can see in your language that there is a little "i" between B and H, so for him there is the BH Army and the HVO. I'm a little lost, because I see that after the word "HVO," we have: "Gorazde, Foca, Trnovo and Visegrad." As far as you know, in Gorazde, was there only the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that sort of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have no knowledge about it. What about Foca and Trnovo and Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I know where these towns are, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, when one reads this document, there were 30 RPGs, mortars, 82 millimetres, 10 of them; M-80, there are 30 pieces, et cetera. It's hard to see how this is distributed between the ABiH and the HVO, because it says for the BH Army and HVO, but regarding those places. So one could believe and infer from that that all the pieces were going to be sent to Gorazde, Foca, Trnovo, and Visegrad. But if there's no ABiH in those four localities, what is the ABiH going to get? That's the question, but you can't answer it, or can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was no more than warehouse-keeper. I didn't look into matters such as these. I wasn't even thinking about that, let alone know anything of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said that you were a warehouse-keeper. Well, I was one, too, when I did my military service. I was in charge of weapons. I would open the boxes and count the weapons, but I would also think whilst doing it. What about you? You can't answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, I can't. I don't have the knowledge, I don't know. I have no specific knowledge for me to be able to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We might see this with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, you said it. There will be a witness coming in this week who will be able to explain that, whether Gorazde, Foca, Trnovo, Visegrad and so on, whether there was any HVO there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But as we're on this document, then we can see, sir, indubitably that two names taking over these weapons, Sulejman Kalidzic and Sahinpasic Senad were the people who took delivery before that. You said Sahinpasic Senad, before that and after that, would take delivery of weapons mostly for the BH Army. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now take a look at the next document, which is 2D898. And we have here the same designation signed by the same man, Mr. Cermak. It is the 24th of November, once again 1992, and it is a donation for the requirements of the 109th Brigade, Doboj. And Mesic, Medzid is mentioned, who is supposed to come and take delivery from Doboj. I want to ask you whether this material reached you in Grude, and according to the distribution order, did you hand it over to Mr. Mesic when he came to collect them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, all these cases were done in the same way. I would act upon the instructions and delivery notices.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the last document in this series is 2D0311. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we're dealing with the 30th of March, 1993. It is authorisation to issue MTS for the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, through the Logistics Base of Grude, and it is signed by the higher advisor, professional advisor, Vladimir Zagorac. This is already an exhibit, but would you look at the last page of the Croatian text of this document, 2D0311. And here we have a fax excerpt, and we can see that it was sent on the 30th of March, 1993, to Bruno Stojic and Safet Orucevic at 0905 hours. Now, do you know which affairs Mr. Safet Orucevic dealt with before that and then --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: For the BH Army, he procured MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We'll just go over the subject of transportation very quickly. And in order to do that, when it comes to permission granted, look at 2D11254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me ask you a question that might appear to be simple, but it might shed light on many things. Looking at this document, the date is the 30th of March. It comes from the Ministry of Defence. It is an order for distribution to the ABiH of military equipment, major equipment, because we have RPG-7s, TNT, et cetera. You, who -- you were in the army, then you were a military man, what do you think; would weapons be given to an enemy, or to friends, or to at least a neutral party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The weapons are given to friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you would tend to give the weapons to your friends. My question was a very basic question, but so was your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's go on, the same topic following on from Judge Antonetti's questions. 2D01254 is the next document number. This is a letter signed by the commander of the 4th Corps, Arif Pasalic. 2D01254 is the number. 01254, yes, that's right. This document, although it's rather illegible, but we can nonetheless see that it's the commander of the 4th Corps, Mr. Arif Pasalic, who has signed it. The date of the document is, as far as we can see in my version, is the 9th of December. Well, anyway, it's December 1992, that's the date, although the day is unclear. And Mr. Pasalic is saying: "Please issue a permit for uninterrupted transport of material and equipment (MTS) via the following route: Mostar-Jablanica-Prozor- Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno-Travnik-Vitez-Visoko and once again Mostar. Tell me, please, Mr. Majic, you haven't seen this document before, have you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But I'm sure you'll be able to clarify some points. What was there in Visoko at that time, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: It was the Central Logistics Base for the BH Army. That was what was in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, the drivers and vehicles are listed for the MTS transport, and then it says, in the middle of the document, transport from Visoko to Mostar departs on the 31st of December, 1992. Now, why was the transport due to depart from Visoko? Is that the Logistics Base?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, this transport going from Visoko to Mostar, we have the following: We have the MTS, and then it says "VST." What is VST?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: It's a recoilless cannon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we see that there were two pieces of those. Then we have mortars, howitzers, mortar barrels, launchers, fuses for mines, and so on. From this document, it follows that permission for the transport of these weapons is being requested; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at the second page, and here it says the HVO Main Staff allowed permission for the MTS transportation to take place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, there's a signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And a stamp too?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, among others, is that the permit granted for each transport?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was standard practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another such document, which is 2D01041, and it dates to March 1993, and this permission was granted and signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic. Yes, the number is correct, 2D01041.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now let's take a look at the next document, which is 2D229. This is a document dated the 26th of February, 1993. It's an exhibit already. I'd like to draw your attention to point 2 of this document, para 2, where Mr. Arif Pasalic says, and he's writing a piece of information to the Staff of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, and here is what he says in point 2, para 2: "Mr. Safet Orucevic successfully performed the main tasks for us until now regarding the entrance of goods with the HVO. He was successful until now." Now, this is Mr. Arif Pasalic writing. To the best of your knowledge, this cooperation between the HVO and the BH Army in certain areas, not to say overall, was it as successful as was stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is based on -- well, we can refer to what I said first, to the effect that Safet Orucevic was the main person for the procurement of MTS for the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Majic, apart from the ways that we have described in which the BH Army procured weapons, which mostly came from the Logistics Base or via the Logistics Base in Grude where you were working, were there any other ways in which the BH Army procured weapons?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. The BH Army used humanitarian convoys as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before the humanitarian convoys, before we get to that, do you know that the BH Army got weapons directly from the Ministry of Defence of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And since you mentioned humanitarian convoys, did you know that the BH Army used humanitarian convoys to receive aid?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I do have knowledge of that, and I have proof and evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What do you know about that? How do you know that the BH Army used humanitarian convoys?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: If it was found that they used humanitarian convoys to carry MTS, our police would seize those materials and equipment, and that would be taken to my warehouse, and they would say who it was taken from, in what way, and so on. And then on the basis of an authorisation from my superior, I would distribute that MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at 2D8, please, and tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This document is dated the 23rd of February, 1993, and we can see that at the Doljani check-point, a vehicle with Gorazde license plates with a trailer was stopped and that it was transporting humanitarian aid for the Merhamet organisation of Gorazde, and that a detailed search was conducted at the Military Police Administration at Ljubuski, and that it was established that apart from the humanitarian aid in the vehicles, there was military equipment found as well. Now, take a look at page 5, I think it is, in your document, and it is page 2D030006 of the Croatian version, which would correspond to page 2D in the English, 030118 onwards. Mr. Majic, we have a list of weapons seized; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then we have photo documentation which shows the type of weapons that were seized; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Majic, is that the convoy that you mentioned a moment ago, when you said that when this MTS was uncovered, it was sent to your warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, finally, Mr. Majic, asked several times by Judge Antonetti, you said that you did not know the answer to some of the questions. You said that you were just a warehouse-keeper during that period, and I'd like to ask you now to explain to the Court how the warehouse in the forest functioned from April 1992 until May 1993, and whether it required your full engagement. How much time did you, in fact, spend in that forest, in that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, day and night, 'round the clock, 24 hours. I was there in the warehouse all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you have to provide security for the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had to take care of security issues for the warehouse, unloading the MTS that were not supposed to get wet.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Now, in the area, was there any way in which you could lock it up, make it secure, store it, or were these MTS accessible to everyone, in view of where they were located?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was out in the open, as I said, so to all intents and purposes accessible, only with the guards securing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, is that why you said that you spent almost 24 hours there, 'round the clock?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR MAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Majic. Thank you, Your Honours. That completes my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I was looking at the photographs of the lorries, the arms that were seized, the reports of questioning of the people who were carrying these items. You said that you saw these weapons, since these were stored in your warehouse.
